title: fix_2117
summary: In the Custom Branding theme editor, picking a named font that happens to be a field's default font (for example **Newsreader** for Book title) used to make the font dropdown snap back to **Default**. Now the dropdown keeps showing the font you actually picked, and choosing **Default** is saved as its own choice. The fonts themselves should look the same as before.

links.label: Issue 2117: Theme editor font dropdown shows "Default" instead of the font you picked

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use a computer, in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. Open the preview with the **Open the preview build** button above. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be finishing: wait a few minutes and reload. If the page still looks like an older version, do a hard refresh: **Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, or **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac.

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Choose **Log in** and sign in with an email address you can check: the app emails you a code to type in. You need to be signed in to make a Custom Branding. A private/incognito window gives you a clean start.

setup.title: Make a Custom Branding and open one of its themes
setup.body: Open **Your content**, click **Create**, and choose **Custom Branding**. Give it a name you'll recognize, for example `Font test`. Under **Themes**, click a theme card to open it (if there are no theme cards, click **Add theme** first). Scroll down to the **Fonts** heading. It has five rows, each with a dropdown: **Default** (ordinary text), **Book title**, **Chapter heading**, **Verse** and **Hebrew subtitle**. Each row also shows a short text sample in the font it's set to.

sections.title: The dropdown shows the font you picked
sections.intro: Each field has a built-in default font. Picking that same font by name used to make the dropdown read "Default".

tests.title: Book title set to Newsreader keeps showing Newsreader
tests.why: This is the exact problem reported in issue 2117. Newsreader is Book title's default font.
steps: In the **Fonts** section, open the **Book title** dropdown.
Choose **Newsreader**.
expected: The sample text next to it is in a serif font (letters with small strokes at the ends), the same as before you changed it.

tests.title: Hebrew subtitle set to Newsreader keeps showing Newsreader
tests.why: Hebrew subtitle's default font is also Newsreader.
steps: Open the **Hebrew subtitle** dropdown.
Choose **Newsreader**.

tests.title: Ordinary text set to System UI keeps showing System UI
tests.why: The first row (labelled **Default**) is for ordinary text, and its default font is System UI.
steps: Open the dropdown in the first row, the one labelled **Default**.
Choose **System UI**.

tests.title: Chapter heading and Verse set to Plus Jakarta Sans keep showing it
tests.why: Both fields default to Plus Jakarta Sans, so the issue says both had the same problem.
steps: Open the **Chapter heading** dropdown and choose **Plus Jakarta Sans**.
Open the **Verse** dropdown and choose **Plus Jakarta Sans**.
expected: The **Chapter heading** dropdown reads **Plus Jakarta Sans**.

tests.title: Your choices are still shown after reloading the page
tests.before: You need the font choices from the four tests above.
steps: Wait a few seconds so the theme saves.
Reload the page (**Ctrl+R** on Windows, **Cmd+R** on Mac).
Open **Your content**, open the `Font test` Custom Branding, open the same theme, and scroll to **Fonts**.

tests.title: Choosing Default shows Default and uses the field's default font
tests.why: Default is now saved as its own choice and turned into the real font only when the theme is shown. If that step went wrong, text would fall back to a plain browser font.
steps: Open the **Book title** dropdown and choose **Playfair Display**. Look at the sample text: it changes to Playfair Display, a tall, high-contrast serif.
Open the **Book title** dropdown again and choose **Default**.
expected: The sample text goes back to looking exactly as it did with **Newsreader** in the first test, not like a plain typewriter or Times New Roman style font.

tests.title: Default stays chosen after reloading
tests.before: You need **Book title** set to **Default** from the test above.
steps: Wait a few seconds, then reload the page.
Open the `Font test` Custom Branding, open the same theme, and scroll to **Fonts**.
expected: **Book title** reads **Default**, and its sample is still in the Newsreader serif font.
The other rows still show what you chose earlier.

tests.title: The reset button puts a field back to Default
steps: Open the **Verse** dropdown and choose **Roboto**.
Next to the **Verse** dropdown, click the reset button (its tooltip or label says **Reset Verse**).
expected: The reset button next to **Verse** disappears.
The sample is back in Plus Jakarta Sans, a clean rounded sans-serif.

tests.title: Default works in a theme based on Dark
tests.why: A field's default font comes from the built-in Light theme. This checks a dark theme still gets real fonts, not a blank fallback.
steps: Go back to the Custom Branding's list of themes and click **Add theme**. The new theme opens.
Near the top of the theme, under **Based on**, choose **Dark**.
Scroll down to **Fonts**.
Set **Book title** to **Cormorant Garamond**, then back to **Default**.
expected: Its sample is in the Newsreader serif font, the same as in the first theme.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: Other named fonts still show and apply as before
steps: In any theme, set **Chapter heading** to **Open Sans**.
Reload the page and reopen the same theme's **Fonts**.
expected: **Chapter heading** reads **Open Sans** and its sample changes to Open Sans, both before and after reloading.

tests.title: A custom Google Font still works
steps: Open the **Hebrew subtitle** dropdown and choose **Custom…**.
In the **Google Font name** box that appears, type `Lexend`.
Wait a few seconds, reload the page, and reopen the same theme's **Fonts**.
expected: The **Hebrew subtitle** dropdown reads **Custom…** and the name box shows `Lexend`, both before and after reloading.
The sample text changes to Lexend (a wide, plain sans-serif).

tests.title: A theme made before this change shows the named font
tests.why: Issue 2117 says themes saved before the fix only remember the font, so a saved font that matches a named option should show as that named option.
tests.before: You need a Custom Branding whose fonts were set before this change (for example one you made in an earlier test round) that you can open in this preview. If you don't have one, mark this test Skip.
steps: Open that older Custom Branding, open one of its themes, and scroll to **Fonts**.
expected: Any row you had set to a named font shows that font's name, even if it is the field's default font (for example **Book title** shows **Newsreader**).
The samples look the same as they did before this change.

notCovered: Older versions of the app (for example the live site before this change ships) opening a theme that was saved with this new version, where a field is set to Default. Those older versions don't know the new way Default is saved.
The font list functions changed for this fix are covered by the automated tests in the PR.
